mostWorthwhile.text: Following fat from large droplets to smaller droplets and then broken molecules was most worthwhile. It made the different jobs of bile and enzymes clear.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the pancreas was least interesting: it advanced the goal but added no explanation beyond the existing picture.

surprise.text: Bile spreads fat into droplets without breaking the fat molecules; enzymes do that afterward. The two-stage result changed how I understood bile's job.

arbitrary.text: None felt purposeless: the pictures showed where the glands' ducts went. The gland fittings were predictable, though, and the pancreas fitting gave little feedback.

continue.text: I would probably continue to see how the small food molecules get into the body. The starch result says glucose can cross the intestinal lining, which leaves a useful next question.
